values: Intransitive movement « monter » generally takes « être » in compound tenses, while transitive « monter quelque chose » takes « avoir ».
Use « montrer quelque chose à quelqu’un » to show something to someone.
« Naviguer » can refer to sailing or navigation generally, as well as browsing online.
« Naître » uses « être » in compound tenses: « il est né »; the past participle agrees with the subject.
« Neiger » is impersonal and is normally used only with « il », as in « il neige ».
Besides watching or noticing, « observer » can mean to comply with or follow a rule, instruction, or period of silence.
« Obtenir » takes a direct object and often means to obtain, secure, or receive something as a result of an effort or process.
Unlike English “obey,” « obéir » takes « à » before the person, rule, or command obeyed.

batch_summary: Added missing senses and notes on auxiliaries, impersonal verbs, and required complements.
